name: Non-saccular Limited Dorsal Myeloschisis

criteria.description: Presence of a midline dorsal skin lesion with a non-saccular stalk connecting skin to spinal cord
MRI evidence of a fibroneural stalk extending from the dorsal spinal cord to the skin lesion without a cystic sac
No presence of saccular myelomeningocele or open neural tube defect
Variable neurological deficits corresponding to spinal cord tethering

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of midline dorsal skin lesion with MRI confirmation of fibroneural stalk connecting skin to spinal cord without saccular cyst
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on MRI imaging and clinical examination of the dorsal midline lesion.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Midline dorsal cutaneous lesion with fibroneural stalk
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic skin lesion directly overlying the spinal cord defect
searchTerms: midline skin lesion with nerve stalk
cutaneous dorsal lesion with fibrous tissue

pathognomonic.symptomName: MRI visualization of fibroneural stalk connecting skin to spinal cord
pathognomonic.notes: Definitive imaging finding distinguishing non-saccular LDM
searchTerms: MRI shows fibrous tissue connecting skin to spine
visible skin to spinal cord connection on MRI

common.notes: Including lower limb weakness or sensory changes

common.symptomName: Cutaneous stigmata such as hypertrichosis or skin dimpling
common.notes: Often present adjacent to the lesion
searchTerms: skin signs like excess hair or dimples
skin patches with unusual hair or pits
cutaneous markers such as hairy spots or skin indentations

common.notes: Neurogenic bladder symptoms due to spinal cord involvement
Variable motor deficits depending on lesion level
searchTerms: spasticity or partial paralysis in lower limbs

occasional.symptomName: Orthopedic deformities such as foot deformities

occasional.notes: May develop due to spinal cord tethering

searchTerms: skin blood vessel malformations near lesion

rare.notes: Rarely associated cystic changes in spinal cord
Rare complication due to skin breakdown

imaging: MRI demonstrating fibroneural stalk connecting dorsal spinal cord to skin lesion without cystic sac
Absence of open neural tube defect or saccular myelomeningocele on imaging
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic occurrence
other: Clinical identification of midline dorsal skin lesion with tethering signs

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of saccular cystic sac over spinal cord
MRI shows cystic lesion rather than fibroneural stalk
Open neural tube defect with exposed neural tissue
Typically associated with large saccular sac and CSF leakage
Often associated with recurrent infections or meningitis

redFlags: Progressive lower limb weakness or paralysis
Signs of spinal cord tethering with neurological deterioration
references: Pang D, Dias MS, Ahab-Barmada M. Limited dorsal myeloschisis: a distinctive clinicopathological entity. Neurosurgery. 1993.
Wang Z, et al. MRI features of limited dorsal myeloschisis: differentiation from other spinal dysraphisms. AJNR Am J Neuroradiol. 2016.
